## HARIDĀSA

He was a disciple of Śyāmānanda Prabhu. (Rasikamaṅgala Dakṣiṇa 1..94)

fields.name: Haridāsa (disciple of Śyāmānanda)
fields.notes:
A disciple of Śyāmānanda Prabhu (Rasika-maṅgala, Dakṣiṇa 1.94; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Haridāsa» 3).

This record («Haridāsa») mixed several persons of the same name; on 05-11-2026 they were separated: Baḍa Haridāsa the kīrtanīya (in «Vāda Haridāsa»), Haridāsa Ācārya (Dvija Haridāsa), the Haridāsa related to Viṭhṭhaleśvara, the padakartā, the disciple of Narottama, and the Haridāsa of Orissa who wrote the Mayūra-candrikā.

fields.works: Six padas in the Padakalpataru (no. 3014: «nācite nā jāni tabu nāciye gaurāṅga bali'»)
fields.notes: A padakartā; six of his songs are in the Padakalpataru, of which no. 3014 is the finest: «I do not know how to dance, yet I dance saying Gaurāṅga; I do not know how to sing, yet I sing» (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Haridāsa» 4).

fields.name: Baḍa Haridāsa
fields.notes:
He belonged to the sakhā of Śrī Caitanya. He was a kīrtana singer and acompanion of Mahāprabhu in Nīlācala (CC. 1.10.147): «Baḍa Haridāsa and Choṭa Haridāsa, two kīrtana singers, stayed with Mahāprabhu».

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Raktaka, a servant of Kṛṣṇa in Vraja (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 138; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Haridāsa» 5). (Choṭa Haridāsa was Patraka.)

A disciple of Narottama Ṭhākura: «Puruṣottama, Gokula dāsa and Haridāsa» (Prema-vilāsa 20); «Glory to Haridāsa, joyful in the rasa of Gaura, always longing to live in Navadvīpa» (Narottama-vilāsa 12; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Haridāsa» 1).

A devotee of Lord Gaurāṅga of Orissa. In the sixteenth century of the Śaka era he wrote the Mayūra-candrikā, with a hymn to Mahāprabhu in its twentieth candrikā (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Haridāsa» 2).

fields.works: Aiśvarya-vivaraṇa, Kāmākhyā-doṣa-vivaraṇa, Ṭippanyāśaya, a ṭīkā on Vallabhācārya's Navaratna-prakāśa, Nirodha-lakṣaṇa-vivṛti, Vedānta-siddhānta-kaumudī, Śruti-kalpadruma, Śloka-pañcaka-vivaraṇa, Siddhānta-rahasya-vṛtti-kārikā, Sevana-bhāvanā-kāvya, Sevā-phala-stotra-vivṛti, Svamārga-dharma-vivaraṇa
fields.notes: A scholar of bhakti-śāstra, a relative of Viṭhṭhaleśvara (the son of Vallabhācārya), who wrote many small works in Sanskrit on bhakti-tattva (Viśvakoṣa, vol. 22, p. 488). He is not Haridāsa Ācārya (Dvija Haridāsa), with whom the record «Haridāsa» mixed him.

fields.aka: Dvija Haridāsa, Dvija Haridāsācārya, Baḍa Haridāsa
fields.notes:
Son of Nṛsiṁha Mukhuṭī, of the brāhmaṇa-kula; a branch of Lord Caitanya: «Śrī Candraśekhara Vaidya, Dvija Haridāsa» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.112). After the Lord's disappearance he wanted to give up his life; the Lord stopped him in a dream and sent him to Vṛndāvana, where he lived as a renunciant. In Vṛndāvana he asked Śrīnivāsa Ācārya to initiate his two sons, Śrīdāsa and Gokulānanda (Bhakti-ratnākara 6.326-327); he passed away on Māgha Kṛṣṇa Ekādaśī soon after Śrīnivāsa left for Gauḍa, and at the festival for him at Kāñcanagaḍiyā Śrīnivāsa initiated the two sons. Their descendants live at Ṭeñā and Sāṭui. The «Śrī Kṛṣṇa-caitanya-sahasra-nāma», from his talks with Narahari Sarakāra, was made known by Lokānandācārya (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Haridāsa Ācārya»).

Sons: Śrīdāsa and Gokulānanda (Gokula dāsa), disciples of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya. Perhaps the same as «Haridāsa Dvija» (470).

Kīrtana singer of Lord Caitanya in Purī, with a very sweet voice: «Baḍa Haridāsa and Choṭa Haridāsa, two kīrtana singers» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.147). For begging rice from Mādhavī Devī the Lord gave him up; after a year he gave up his life at Prayāga and went on singing for the Lord unseen (Antya 2.100-165). Not Laghu Haridāsa.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Patraka, a servant of Kṛṣṇa in Vraja (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 138; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Haridāsa» 6).
